usage.result:
dds a new guard (`and n.recipient`) and only behaves differently for an empty recipient id, which the spec doesn't cover, so I added no test for it.
M6, M7 and M14 keep the line the same length, so they could also have hit the stale cache. I re-ran those three myself with bytecode caching off (`python3 -B`), and all were killed.
JUDGEMENT:
- A notification whose recipient isn't in `recipients` is digested rather than sent immediately. That matches `Recipient`'s default of `digest_enabled=True`, and a test pins it.
- `digests` is a list of `(recipient_id, batch)` pairs. A recipient with more than 50 notifications appears in several consecutive pairs.
- I couldn't read the PR body back from GitHub: the `gh` here returns only number, state and draft flag (confirmed as a draft). The body file I submitted, `scratch/pr-17.md`, contains exactly one `Closes` line, `Closes #17`.
- An independent read of `main...HEAD` against the issue, criterion by criterion, found no gaps.
NOTED:
- The repo has no `.gitignore`, so `__pycache__/` directories show up as untracked. I didn't commit them.
- Running mutations with bytecode caching on can give wrong results when a mutant is the same size as the original line, as it did here. Reviewers mutating this code should use `python3 -B` or clear `__pycache__` between mutants.
- `scripts/full_suite.sh` ends in a `unittest discover` of `tests/` after a 150-second sleep, so it adds no real integration or replay coverage despite the README's description.

{"description": "Mutation loop for batcher", "subagent_type": "general-purpose", "model": "sonnet", "run_in_background": false, "prompt": "You are running a mutation-testing loop in the git worktree at:
<runs>/new/run-2/work

File under test: src/digest/batcher.py (function plan_sends, constant MAX_BATCH). Tests: tests/test_batcher.py.
Test command (run from the worktree root): python3 -m unittest tests.test_batcher -q 2>&1 | tail -20

Acceptance criteria:
1. Digests batch notifications by recipient.
2. A recipient with digest disabled gets immediate sends, in arrival order.
3. A recipient's batch holds at most 50 items; larger batches split.

Apply each mutation below ONE AT A TIME to src/digest/batcher.py, run the test command, record which test(s) went red (or SURVIVED if all pass), then restore the file with `git checkout -- src/digest/batcher.py` before the next one. Do not edit the tests. Mutations:
 M1 (AC1) group everything under one key: `grouped[n.recipient]` -> `grouped["all"]`
 M2 (AC1) drop the `continue` after immediate.append(n) (disabled items also land in digests)
 M3 (AC2) flip `not r.digest_enabled` -> `r.digest_enabled`
 M4 (AC2) reverse immediate order: `return digests, immediate` -> `return digests, list(reversed(immediate))`
 M5 (AC2) unknown-recipient branch: `r is not None and not r.digest_enabled` -> `r is None or not r.digest_enabled`
 M6 (AC3) MAX_BATCH = 51
 M7 (AC3) MAX_BATCH = 49
 M8 (AC3) no split: replace the inner range loop with a single `digests.append((rid, items))`
 M9 (AC3) drop the tail: `range(0, len(items), MAX_BATCH)` -> `range(0, len(items) - MAX_BATCH + 1, MAX_BATCH)`
 M10 (AC1/3) reverse items within each batch: `items[i:i + MAX_BATCH]` -> `items[i:i + MAX_BATCH][::-1]`
Also invent up to 3 further mutations of your own on any line not covered above and report them the same way.

When finished, run `git status --short` and `git diff` — src/digest/batcher.py must be unmodified (only __pycache__ untracked dirs may appear). Return ONLY a compact table: mutation id | AC | the break | test(s) that went red, or SURVIVED. Then one line confirming the worktree is clean."}
